## Athletics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Chicago&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Athletics")]

Main article: [UIC Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIC_Flames "UIC Flames")

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/UIC_pavilion_%28Chicago%2C_USA%29.JPG/250px-UIC_pavilion_%28Chicago%2C_USA%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UIC_pavilion_(Chicago,_USA).JPG)

[Credit Union 1 Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_Union_1_Arena "Credit Union 1 Arena")

The Illinois–Chicago (UIC) athletic teams are called the Flames, a reference to the [1871 Great Chicago Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1871_Great_Chicago_Fire "1871 Great Chicago Fire"). The university is a member of the [Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") level of the [National Collegiate Athletic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association") (NCAA), primarily competing in the [Missouri Valley Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Valley_Conference "Missouri Valley Conference") (MVC) since the 2022–23 academic year.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Chicago#cite_note-89) The Flames previously competed in the D-I [Horizon League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horizon_League "Horizon League") from 1994–95 to 2021–22; in the D-I [Mid-Continent Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_League "Summit League") (Mid-Con, now currently known as the Summit League since the 2007–08 school year) from 1982–83 to 1993–94; as an [NCAA D-I Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_independent_schools "NCAA Division I independent schools") during the 1981–82 school year; and in the [Chicagoland Collegiate Athletic Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicagoland_Collegiate_Athletic_Conference "Chicagoland Collegiate Athletic Conference") (CCAC) of the [National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Intercollegiate_Athletics "National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics") (NAIA) from 1949–50 to about 1980–81.

UIC competes in 18 intercollegiate varsity sports:[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Chicago#cite_note-90) Men's sports include baseball, basketball, cross country, soccer, swimming & diving, tennis and track & field (indoor and outdoor); while women's sports include basketball, cross country, golf, soccer, softball, swimming & diving, tennis, track & field (indoor and outdoor) and volleyball.

### Men's soccer

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Chicago&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Men's soccer")]

In September 2006, the men's soccer team earned its highest ranking in school history when the SoccerTimes.com College Coaches Poll pegged the Flames at No. 6 in the country. In November 2006, UIC defeated Western Illinois 3–0 in the opening round of the NCAA tournament before falling in the second round to Notre Dame 1–0. UIC finished the 2006 season as the nation's best defensive squad after allowing a mere eight goals in over 1993 minutes of play during 21 matches for a goals-against average (GAA) of 0.36. The GAA was tops in the nation in 2006 and it also ranked fifth all-time in NCAA history. UIC posted 13 shutouts and never allowed more than a single goal in a match. UIC also allowed just two goals after intermission the entire season. Along with the GAA mark, UIC posted the nation's best save percentage with a 0.908 rate.

In 2007, UIC soccer's successful season culminated in an Elite-Eight appearance in the NCAA tournament by way of wins over No. 12 St. Louis, Northwestern, and No. 8 Creighton. In a bid for a Final-Four appearance, UIC fell to Massachusetts 2–1. At season's end, UIC had a record of 13–6–6 and was named a top 10 team by the [National Soccer Coaches Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Soccer_Coaches "United Soccer Coaches") (NSCAA).

### Baseball

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Chicago&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Baseball")]

UIC's baseball team recorded 30 or more victories in a nine-year stretch from 2001 to 2010, won seven straight Horizon League Championships, and advanced to an NCAA regional four times (2003, 2005, 2007, 2008). UIC baseball has recorded regional wins against No. 1 Long Beach State in 2007 and No. 2 Dallas Baptist University in 2008.

### Gymnastics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Chicago&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Gymnastics")]

In 1978 and 1979 the UIC men's gymnastics team won the school's only NCAA team titles at the Division II Championships. Following the 1979 season the men's gymnastics program entered Division I competition and finished the season ranked 10th, Nationally. After the successful 1980 season the remainder of the UIC athletic teams ascended to Division I status. The 1996 men's gymnastics team finished the season in 9th place, the school's highest final ranking among all sports. UIC Men's Gymnastics individual Division I All America honorees include: Paul Fina (Rings), Mike Costa (Pommel Horse, twice), Barry McDonald (Parallel Bars), Shannon Welker (Floor Exercise), Neil Faustino (Vault), and Andrew Stover (Horizontal Bar).

# Tagged: University of Illinois Chicago

[](link_14)

### [University of Illinois Chicago Social Work Dean to Retire After 35 Years of Service](link_14)

June 5, 2026

Creasie Finney Hairston, a leading scholar on the impact of incarceration on families, has led the Jane Addams College of Social Work at the University of Illinois Chicago for the past 35 years. She is slated to retire on December 15.

[](link_15)

### [Barbara Ransby Receives National Award for Contributions to American History Research](link_15)

May 8, 2026

The Organization of American Historians has honored the University of Illinois Chicago's Barbara Ransby for her decades of scholarship, mentorship, and public engagement. Her work has helped shape the study of African American history, social movements, and Black feminist thought.

[](link_16)

### [Seven Black Scholars Elected to the National Academy of Education](link_16)

February 4, 2026

The National Academy of Education has elected 19 distinguished education scholars and leaders to its membership. Of the 19 new members of the National Academy of Education, it appears that seven are African Americans.

[](link_17)

### [In Memoriam: Jamie Theresa Phelps, 1941-2025](link_17)

January 6, 2026

As director of the Institute for Black Catholic Studies at Xavier University of Louisiana, Dr. Phelps challenged the Catholic Church to better understand itself through the voices and experiences of Black Catholics and those on the margins.

[](link_18)

### [In Memoriam: Marcyliena H. Morgan, 1950-2025](link_18)

October 14, 2025

Dr. Morgan was a professor of African and African American studies and the Ernest E. Monrad Professor of Social Sciences at Harvard. While there, she founded the Hip Hop Archive and Research Institute in the university's Hutchins Center for African and African American Research.

[](link_19)

### [Higher Education Gifts or Grants of Interest to African Americans](link_19)

October 16, 2024

Here is this week’s news of grants or gifts to historically Black colleges and universities or for programs of particular interest to African Americans in higher education.

[](link_20)

### [Study Uncovers Racial Bias in University Admissions and Decision-Making AI Algorithms](link_20)

July 22, 2024

A new study has found university admissions and decision-making AI algorithms incorrectly predict academic failure for Black students 19 percent of the time, compared to 12 percent of White students and 6 percent of Asian students.

[](link_21)

### [The Eutychus Phenomenon](link_21)

July 17, 2024

Part of the Eutychus phenomenon is viewing those with diverse viewpoints in the room as fortunate, but not vital contributors. The narrative that affirmative action scours the earth looking for inept candidates to give them what mediocre White people rightfully deserve is oft repeated and sadly, embraced by many.

[](link_22)

### [University of Illinois Professor Ruby Mendenhall Named Poet Laureate](link_22)

April 1, 2024

Dr. Mendenhall currently serves as the Kathryn Lee Baynes Dallenbach Professor in Liberal Arts and Sciences at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign where she teaches sociology, African American studies, and urban and regional planning.

[](link_23)

### [Exposure to Lead Among Children Has Declined But a Racial Gap Remains](link_23)

January 22, 2024

Lead is a naturally occurring metal that can cause serious health effects if it accumulates in the blood. Young children are particularly vulnerable, as lead can damage their developing brains and contribute to learning or behavioral problems.

### [Raphael Florestal-Kevelier Selected to Lead the American College Health Association](link_24)

June 26, 2023

Raphael Florestal-Kevelie is the assistant vice chancellor for student health and wellness and a clinical assistant professor of community health sciences in the School of Public Health at the University of Illinois Chicago. The American College Health Association has 750 higher education member institutions representing nearly 10,000 members.

[](link_25)

### [Three Black Scholars Taking on New Faculty Roles at Universities](link_25)

June 16, 2023

Dwight A. McBride was appointed the inaugural Gerald Early Distinguished Professor at Washington University in St. Louis. Fanta Waterman has been appointed a clinical assistant professor in the School of Public Health at the University of Illinois Chicago and Ahkinyala Abdullah, an associate professor of environmental science and ecology, was named director of the Union National Research Institute at Virginia Union University.

### [Vanderbilt University Scholar Has Established the “Possibilities Project”](link_26)

June 7, 2023

The Possibilities Project, under the direction of Chezare Warren, an associate professor of leadership policy, and organizations at Vanderbilt’s Peabody College of education and human development “is an arts-informed knowledge hub committed to improving Black students’ well-being in education and beyond.”

### [Miriam Mobley Smith Honored by the American Society of Health-Systems Pharmacists](link_27)

January 27, 2023

Miriam Mobley Smith is the interim dean of the Daniel K. Inouye College of Pharmacy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo. Prior to coming to the University of Hawai'i in 2021, the veteran pharmacy academic served as interim dean and visiting professor at the Northeastern University Bourvé College of Health Sciences in Boston and as dean and tenured professor at the Chicago State University College of Pharmacy.

[](https://jbhe.com/2021/05/university-of-illinois-chicago-strips-the-name-of-john-marshall-from-its-law-school/ "University of Illinois Chicago Strips the Name of John Marshall From Its Law School")

### [University of Illinois Chicago Strips the Name of John Marshall From Its Law School](https://jbhe.com/2021/05/university-of-illinois-chicago-strips-the-name-of-john-marshall-from-its-law-school/ "University of Illinois Chicago Strips the Name of John Marshall From Its Law School")

May 26, 2021

John Marshall served as Chief Justice of the United States from 1801 to 1835. But research showed that he was a slave trader, enslaved hundreds of African Americans, was the author of pro-slavery judicial opinions, and held racist views.

[](link_28)

### [Four African Americans Scholars Appointed to University Dean Positions](link_28)

April 5, 2021

The new deans are Trisha Clement-Montgomery at the University of Kentucky, Darryl Scriven at Clarkson University in Potsdam, New York, Denise Stephens at the University of Oklahoma, and Rhea Ballard-Thrower at the University of Illinois at Chicago.

[](link_29)

### [Four African Americans Who Are Leaving Their High-Level Posts at State Universities](link_29)

April 30, 2019

The four African American who are stepping down from their positions are Ellen Smiley at Grambling State University in Louisiana, Neema Connor at the University of Maryland Eastern Shore, Dana Brooks at West Virginia University, and Melvin Leon Heard at the University of Illinois at Chicago.

### [Seven Black Scholars Taking on New Assignments at Colleges and Universities](link_31)

June 29, 2018

Taking on new roles are Amy Freeman at Penn State, Juana Mendenhall at Morehouse College, Cynthia Blair at the University of Illinois-Chicago, Lawrence Bobo at Harvard University, Princess U II Imoukhuede at Washington University, Dwana Waugh at Sweet Briar College, and Diane Edison at Hollins University.

### [Racial Differences in How Long Students Take to Earn an Undergraduate Degree](https://jbhe.com/2026/10/racial-differences-in-how-long-students-take-to-earn-an-undergraduate-degree/ "Racial Differences in How Long Students Take to Earn an Undergraduate Degree")

October 5, 2026

Among Black students who earned an undergraduate award (bachelor's degrees, associate degrees, or certificates) in 2024–2025, those attending HBCUs completed their program faster than those attending other institutions.

[](https://jbhe.com/2026/10/the-majority-of-voters-believe-race-relations-in-the-u-s-are-getting-worse/ "The Majority of Voters Believe Race Relations in the U.S. Are Getting Worse")

### [The Majority of Voters Believe Race Relations in the U.S. Are Getting Worse](https://jbhe.com/2026/10/the-majority-of-voters-believe-race-relations-in-the-u-s-are-getting-worse/ "The Majority of Voters Believe Race Relations in the U.S. Are Getting Worse")

October 5, 2026

The **University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign** (**UIUC**, **U of I**, **Illinois**, or **University of Illinois**) is a [public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_university "Public university")[land-grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land-grant_university "Land-grant university")[research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in the [Champaign–Urbana metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign%E2%80%93Urbana_metropolitan_area "Champaign–Urbana metropolitan area"), Illinois, United States. Established in 1867, it is the founding campus and [flagship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagship#Colleges_and_universities_in_the_United_States "Flagship") institution of the [University of Illinois System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_System "University of Illinois System"). With over 59,000 students, the University of Illinois is one of the [largest public universities by enrollment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_public_university_campuses_by_enrollment "List of United States public university campuses by enrollment") in the United States.

The university contains 16 schools and colleges[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-9) and offers more than 150 undergraduate and over 100 graduate programs of study. The university holds 651 buildings on 6,370 acres (2,578 ha)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Illinois_Facts-6) and its annual operating budget in 2016 was over $2 billion.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-10) The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign also operates [a research park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_Park_at_the_University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign "Research Park at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign") home to innovation centers for over 90 start-up companies and [multinational corporations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-research.illinois.edu-11)

The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign is a member of the [Association of American Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities "Association of American Universities") and is [classified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Classification_of_Institutions_of_Higher_Education "Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education") among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Carnegie-12) In fiscal year 2019, research expenditures at Illinois totaled $652 million.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-2018_R&D-13)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-research.illinois.edu-11) The campus library system possesses the [fourth-largest university library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_libraries_in_the_United_States "University libraries in the United States") in the United States by holdings.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-14) The university also hosts the [National Center for Supercomputing Applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Center_for_Supercomputing_Applications "National Center for Supercomputing Applications").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-15)

The alumni, faculty members, or researchers of the university include 24 [Nobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") laureates, 27 [Pulitzer Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize "Pulitzer Prize") winners, 2 [Fields medalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fields_Medal "Fields Medal"), and 2 [Turing Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Award "Turing Award") winners. Illinois athletic teams compete in [Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") of the [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association") and are collectively known as the [Fighting Illini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Fighting_Illini "Illinois Fighting Illini"). They are members of the [Big Ten Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference "Big Ten Conference") and have won the [second-most conference titles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference#Conference_titles "Big Ten Conference"). [Illinois Fighting Illini football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Fighting_Illini_football "Illinois Fighting Illini football") won the [Rose Bowl Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Bowl_Game "Rose Bowl Game") in 1947, 1952, 1964 and a total of five national championships. Illinois athletes have won 29 medals in [Olympic events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign "History of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign")

### Illinois Industrial University (1867–1885)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Illinois Industrial University (1867–1885)")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/IllinoisIndustrialUniversity.jpg/250px-IllinoisIndustrialUniversity.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:IllinoisIndustrialUniversity.jpg)

University Hall stood from 1871 until 1938 and was replaced by Gregory Hall and the [Illini Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illini_Union "Illini Union"). Pieces were used in the erection of Hallene Gateway.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-16)

The University of Illinois, originally named "Illinois Industrial University", was one of the 37 universities created under the first [Morrill Land-Grant Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morrill_Land-Grant_Acts "Morrill Land-Grant Acts"), which provided public land for the creation of agricultural and industrial colleges and universities across the United States. Among several cities, [Urbana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbana,_Illinois "Urbana, Illinois") was selected in 1867 as the site for the new school.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Illini_years_pg6-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-University_of_Illinois_Archives-18) From the beginning, President [John Milton Gregory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Milton_Gregory "John Milton Gregory")'s desire to establish an institution firmly grounded in the [liberal arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_arts "Liberal arts") tradition was at odds with many state residents and lawmakers who wanted the university to offer classes based solely around "industrial education".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-manifesto-19) The university opened for classes on March 2, 1868, and had two faculty members and 77 students.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-story-20)

The library, which opened with the school in 1868, started with 1,039 volumes. Subsequently, President [Edmund J. James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_J._James "Edmund J. James"), in a speech to the board of trustees in 1912, proposed to create a research library. It is now one of the world's largest public academic collections.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-University_of_Illinois_Archives-18)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-illinois2-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-About_the_University_Library-22) In 1870, the Mumford House was constructed as a model farmhouse for the school's experimental farm. The Mumford House remains the oldest structure on campus.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-23) The original University Hall (1871) was the fourth building built; it stood where the Illini Union stands today.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-UIHistories-24)

The University of Illinois' Undergraduate Library (UGL) was constructed underground to preserve open space on campus and to prevent casting shadows on the adjacent Morrow Plots, the oldest continually used experimental agricultural fields in the United States.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-25) This unique design inspired The Other Guys, a student a cappella group, to create the "Morrow Plots Song," humorously explaining that the library was built underground "'Cause you can't throw shade on the corn". [[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-26) The song has become a beloved piece among students and alumni, celebrating the university's history and traditions.

### University of Illinois (1885–1977)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: University of Illinois (1885–1977)")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/University_of_Illinois_1900.jpg/250px-University_of_Illinois_1900.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:University_of_Illinois_1900.jpg)

Full Membership certificate of the University of Illinois, issued 22 March 1900

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Alma-front.jpg/250px-Alma-front.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alma-front.jpg)

_[Alma Mater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alma\_Mater\_(Illinois\_sculpture) "Alma Mater (Illinois sculpture)")_ by [Lorado Taft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorado_Taft "Lorado Taft"), located in front of [Altgeld Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altgeld_Hall "Altgeld Hall")

In 1885, the Illinois Industrial University officially changed its name to the "University of Illinois", reflecting its agricultural, mechanical, and liberal arts curriculum.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-manifesto-19) According to educational historian [Roger L. Geiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_L._Geiger "Roger L. Geiger"), Illinois and a few other public and private universities set the standard for what the [research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in the United States would become.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Crow-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Geiger_Page_3-28) During his presidency, [Edmund J. James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_J._James "Edmund J. James") (1904–1920) set the policy of building a massive research library.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Solberg-I-67-29) He also laid the foundation for the large Chinese international student population on campus.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-IAM-30) James established ties with China through the Chinese Minister to the United States [Wu Ting-Fang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu_Tingfang "Wu Tingfang"). Also during James's time in 1916, [St. Elmo Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Elmo_Brady "St. Elmo Brady") became the first African American nationally to earn a [Ph.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ph.D. "Ph.D.") in [Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry "Chemistry").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-31) Class rivalries and [Bob Zuppke's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Zuppke "Robert Zuppke") winning football teams contributed to campus morale.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-University_of_Illinois_Archives-18)

[_Alma Mater_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alma_Mater_(Illinois_sculpture) "Alma Mater (Illinois sculpture)"), a prominent statue on campus created by alumnus [Lorado Taft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorado_Taft "Lorado Taft"), was unveiled on June 11, 1929. It was funded from donations by the Alumni Fund and the classes of 1923–1929.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Alma_Mater-32)

The [Great Depression in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression_in_the_United_States "Great Depression in the United States") slowed construction and expansion on the campus. The university replaced the original university hall with Gregory Hall and the [Illini Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illini_Union "Illini Union"). After World War II, the university experienced rapid growth. The enrollment doubled and the academic standing improved.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-33) This period was also marked by large growth in the Graduate College and increased federal support of scientific and technological research. During the 1950s and 1960s the university experienced the turmoil common on many American campuses. Among these were the water fights of the 1950s and 1960s.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-34)

### University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1977–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1977–present)")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/UIUCEngineeringHall.jpg/250px-UIUCEngineeringHall.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UIUCEngineeringHall.jpg)

Engineering Hall is located along Boneyard Creek on the Engineering Campus.

By 1967, the [University of Illinois system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_system "University of Illinois system") consisted of a main campus in Champaign-Urbana and two Chicago campuses, Chicago Circle (UICC) and Medical Center (UIMC), and people began using "Urbana-Champaign" or the reverse to refer to the main campus specifically. The university name officially changed to the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign by 1977 (although the word "at" was later dropped for marketing purposes by all U of I System campuses by 2021). While this was a reversal of the commonly used designation for the metropolitan area ([Champaign-Urbana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign-Urbana "Champaign-Urbana")), a majority of the campus is located in Urbana. The name change established a separate identity for the main campus within the [University of Illinois System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_System "University of Illinois System"), which today includes separate institutions at the [University of Illinois Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Chicago "University of Illinois Chicago") (formed by the merger of UICC and UIMC) and [University of Illinois Springfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Springfield "University of Illinois Springfield").

In 1998, the Hallene Gateway Plaza was dedicated. The Plaza features the original sandstone portal of University Hall, which was originally the fourth building on campus.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-UIHistories-24) In recent years, state support has declined from 4.5% of the state's tax appropriations in 1980 to 2.28% in 2011, a nearly 50% decline.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-35) As a result, the university's budget has shifted away from relying on state support with nearly 84% of the budget coming from other sources in 2012.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Budget_by_Source_of_Funds-36)

On March 12, 2015, the Board of Trustees approved the creation of a medical school, the first college created at Urbana-Champaign in 60 years.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-chicagotribune.com-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-news.illinois.edu-39) The [Carle Illinois College of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carle_Illinois_College_of_Medicine "Carle Illinois College of Medicine") began classes in 2018.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-40) It is the world's first engineering-based medical school.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-41)

## Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Campus")]

Main article: [Campus of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campus_of_the_University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign "Campus of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign")

See also: [Campustown (Champaign, Illinois)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campustown_(Champaign,_Illinois) "Campustown (Champaign, Illinois)")

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/GreenStreetCampustownChampaignIllinois.JPG/250px-GreenStreetCampustownChampaignIllinois.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GreenStreetCampustownChampaignIllinois.JPG)

Green Street in [Campustown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campustown_(Champaign,_Illinois) "Campustown (Champaign, Illinois)")

The main research and academic facilities are divided almost evenly between the twin cities of [Urbana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbana,_Illinois "Urbana, Illinois") and [Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign,_Illinois "Champaign, Illinois"), which form part of the [Champaign–Urbana metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign%E2%80%93Urbana_metropolitan_area "Champaign–Urbana metropolitan area"). Some parts are in [Urbana Township](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbana_Township,_Champaign_County,_Illinois "Urbana Township, Champaign County, Illinois").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-42)

Four main quads compose the center of the university and are arranged from north to south. The Beckman Quadrangle and the [John Bardeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bardeen "John Bardeen") Quadrangle occupy the center of the [Engineering Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIUC_Engineering_Campus "UIUC Engineering Campus"). [Boneyard Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boneyard_Creek "Boneyard Creek") flows through the John Bardeen Quadrangle, parallel to Green Street. The Beckman Quadrangle, named after [Arnold Orville Beckman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Orville_Beckman "Arnold Orville Beckman"), is primarily composed of research units and laboratories, and features a large solar calendar consisting of an obelisk and several copper fountains. The Main Quadrangle and South Quadrangle follow immediately after the John Bardeen Quad. The former makes up a large part of the [Liberal Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIUC_College_of_Liberal_Arts_and_Sciences "UIUC College of Liberal Arts and Sciences") portion of the campus, while the latter comprises many of the buildings of the [College of Agriculture, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIUC_College_of_Agriculture,_Consumer,_and_Environmental_Sciences "UIUC College of Agriculture, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences") (ACES) spread across the campus map.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-43)

Additionally, the research fields of the College of ACES stretch south from Urbana and Champaign into [Savoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savoy,_Illinois "Savoy, Illinois") and [Champaign County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign_County,_Illinois "Champaign County, Illinois"). The university also maintains formal gardens and a conference center in nearby [Monticello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monticello,_Illinois "Monticello, Illinois") at [Allerton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Allerton_Park "Robert Allerton Park").

The campus is known for its landscape and architecture, as well as distinctive landmarks.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-44) It was identified as one of 50 college or university "works of art" by T.A. Gaines in his book _The Campus as a Work of Art_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-45) The campus also has a number of buildings and sites on the [U.S. National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") including [Harker Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harker_Hall "Harker Hall"), the [Astronomical Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronomical_Observatory_(University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign) "Astronomical Observatory (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)"), [Louise Freer Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louise_Freer_Hall "Louise Freer Hall"), the [Main Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Library_(University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign) "Main Library (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)"), the [Experimental Dairy Farm Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Experimental_Dairy_Farm_Historic_District "University of Illinois Experimental Dairy Farm Historic District"), and the [Morrow Plots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morrow_Plots "Morrow Plots"). [University of Illinois Willard Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Willard_Airport "University of Illinois Willard Airport") is one of the few airports owned by an educational institution.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-46)

[Chesterbrook Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesterbrook_Academy?action=edit&redlink=1 "Chesterbrook Academy (page does not exist)") private preschool, which opened in 2007, is located on the campus and serves infants through Pre-K.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-48)

### Sustainability

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Sustainability")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/UIUC_morrow_plot.JPG/250px-UIUC_morrow_plot.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UIUC_morrow_plot.JPG)

[Morrow Plots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morrow_Plots "Morrow Plots") in front of the [Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_R._Woese_Institute_for_Genomic_Biology "Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology")

In 2008, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign became a signatory of the American College and University Presidents' Climate Commitment, binding the campus to the goal of [carbon neutrality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_neutrality "Carbon neutrality") as soon as possible. In 2010, the first Illinois Climate Action Plan (iCAP) was written to chart a path to this goal. The iCAP is a strategic framework for meeting the university's Climate Leadership Commitments to be carbon-neutral by 2050 or sooner and build resilience with its local community. Since then, the iCAP has been rewritten every five years to track the university's progress.

In December 2013, the University of Illinois launched the Institute for Sustainability, Energy, and Environment (iSEE) on the Urbana-Champaign campus. The institute, under the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation, leads an interdisciplinary approach to researching solutions for the world's most pressing sustainability, energy, and environmental needs. In addition, iSEE has engaged students, faculty, staff, and campus leadership in the iCAP process — especially in the areas of zero waste and conservation of energy, food, water, land, and natural resources — as well as sustainability outreach and immersive educational programs.

In 2022, new solar and geothermal energy projects, a reduction in water use, and wide-ranging sustainability research helped the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign earn its fifth consecutive gold certification in the [Sustainability Tracking, Assessment & Rating System (STARS)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainability_Tracking,_Assessment_&_Rating_System "Sustainability Tracking, Assessment & Rating System").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-49) Illinois has consistently achieved gold certification since it began reporting data through STARS in 2013, and the 2022 score was one of its highest to date.

Currently, the campus features 27 LEED-certified buildings.

### Online learning

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Online learning")]

In addition to the university's Illinois Online platform, in 2015 the university entered into a partnership with the Silicon Valley educational technology company [Coursera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coursera "Coursera") to offer a series of master's degrees, certifications, and specialization courses, currently including more than 70 joint learning classes. In August 2015, the Master of Business Administration program was launched through the platform.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-68) On March 31, 2016, Coursera announced the launch of the Master of Computer Science in Data Science from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-69) At the time, the university's computer-science graduate program was ranked fifth in the United States by _[U.S. News & World Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S.\_News\_&\_World\_Report "U.S. News & World Report")_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-70) On March 29, 2017, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign launched their Master's in Accounting (iMSA) program, now called the Master of Science in Accountancy (iMSA) program. The iMSA program is led through live sessions, headed by Illinois faculty.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-71)

Similar to the university's on-campus admission policies, the online master's degrees offered by the U of I through Coursera also has admission requirements. All applicants must hold a bachelor's degree, and have earned a 3.0 GPA or higher in the last two years of study. Additionally, all applicants must prove their proficiency in English.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-coursera.org-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-73)

The U of I also offers online courses in partnership with Coursera, such as Marketing in a Digital World, which focuses on how digital tools like internet, smartphone and 3D printers are changing the marketing landscape.

[Round barns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round_barns_in_Illinois "Round barns in Illinois") on the [University of Illinois Experimental Dairy Farm Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Experimental_Dairy_Farm_Historic_District "University of Illinois Experimental Dairy Farm Historic District"), part of [ACES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIUC_College_of_Agriculture,_Consumer,_and_Environmental_Sciences "UIUC College of Agriculture, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences")

The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign is often regarded as a world-leading magnet for engineering and sciences (both applied and basic).[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-95) According to the [National Science Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Science_Foundation "National Science Foundation"), the university spent $625 million on research and development in 2018, ranking it 37th in the nation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-2018_R&D-13)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-research.illinois.edu-11) It is also listed as one of the top 25 American research universities by [The Center for Measuring University Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Center_for_Measuring_University_Performance "The Center for Measuring University Performance").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-96)

Besides the annual influx of grants and sponsored projects, the university manages an extensive modern research infrastructure.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-97) The university has been a leader in computer-based education and hosted the [PLATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLATO_(computer_system) "PLATO (computer system)") project, which was a precursor to the internet and resulted in the development of the [plasma display](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_display "Plasma display"). Illinois was a 2nd-generation [ARPAnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARPAnet "ARPAnet") site in 1971 and was the first institution to license the [UNIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNIX "UNIX") operating system from Bell Labs. In [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates")' 2004 talk as part of his five-university campus tour titled "Software Breakthroughs: Solving the Toughest Problems in Computer Science,"[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-98) he mentioned that [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") hired more graduates from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign than from any other university in the world.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-99)

The [Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beckman_Institute_for_Advanced_Science_and_Technology "Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology") is the largest interdisciplinary facility on campus, at 313,000 square feet (29,100 m 2).

The university hosts the [National Center for Supercomputing Applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Center_for_Supercomputing_Applications "National Center for Supercomputing Applications") (NCSA), which created [Mosaic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosaic_(web_browser) "Mosaic (web browser)"), the first graphical [web browser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_browser "Web browser"), the [Apache HTTP server](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_HTTP_server "Apache HTTP server"), and [NCSA Telnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCSA_Telnet "NCSA Telnet"). The Parallel@Illinois program hosts several programs in [parallel computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_computing "Parallel computing"), including the [Universal Parallel Computing Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPCRC_Illinois "UPCRC Illinois"). The university contracted with [Cray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cray "Cray") to build the [National Science Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Science_Foundation "National Science Foundation")-funded supercomputer [Blue Waters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Waters "Blue Waters").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-102) The system also has the largest public online storage system in the world with more than 25 petabytes of usable space.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-103) The university celebrated January 12, 1997, as the "birthday" of [HAL 9000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_9000 "HAL 9000"), the fictional supercomputer from the novel and film _2001: A Space Odyssey_; in both works, HAL credits "Urbana, Illinois" as his place of operational origin.

The [Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beckman_Institute_for_Advanced_Science_and_Technology "Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology") supports interdisciplinary collaborative research in the broad areas of intelligent systems, neuroscience, molecular science and engineering, and biomedical imaging.

The [Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_R._Woese_Institute_for_Genomic_Biology "Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology") supports research in genomics and related areas of biology.

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/UofIPrarieResearch.JPG/250px-UofIPrarieResearch.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UofIPrarieResearch.JPG)

One of the university's research [prairie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prairie "Prairie") fields, located off Florida Avenue

The [Prairie Research Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prairie_Research_Institute "Prairie Research Institute") on campus houses several divisions, including the [Illinois Natural History Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Natural_History_Survey "Illinois Natural History Survey"), Illinois State Geological Survey, Illinois State Water Survey, Illinois Sustainable Technology Center, and Illinois State Archaeological Survey. Researchers focus on areas such as agriculture, biodiversity, climate, public health, emerging pests, energy, mineral resources, pollution mitigation, and water resources. The Illinois Natural History Survey holds extensive collections, including one of North America's largest insect collections. The Illinois State Geological Survey manages the Illinois Geological Samples Library and paleontological collections. The Illinois State Archaeological Survey preserves a large collection of Illinois archaeological artifacts, including those from the [Cahokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cahokia "Cahokia") Mounds.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-104)

The Technology Entrepreneur Center at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign offers resources for students to develop their entrepreneurial ideas, including classes, competitions, and workshops.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-105) It hosts events including the Cozad New Venture Challenge, Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Workshop, Illinois I-Corps, and SocialFuse. The Cozad Challenge, held annually since 2000, provides mentorship and workshops on venture creation, with teams competing for funding.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-106) The Silicon Valley Workshop, a week-long event in January, exposes students to startups, technology companies, and entrepreneurial alumni in [Silicon Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon_Valley "Silicon Valley").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-107) Illinois I-Corps helps National Science Foundation grantees identify valuable product opportunities from academic research through customer discovery and entrepreneurship training.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-109) SocialFuse is a pitching and networking event where students can present ideas and connect with potential teammates.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-110)

The Center for Plasma-Material Interactions was established in 2004 by Professor David N. Ruzic to research the complex behavior between [ions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion "Ion"), [electrons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron "Electron"), and [energetic atoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energetic_neutral_atom "Energetic neutral atom") generated in [plasmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_(physics) "Plasma (physics)") and the surfaces of materials. CPMI encompasses [fusion plasmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_fusion "Nuclear fusion") in its research.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-113)

In 2007, the university-hosted research [Institute for Condensed Matter Theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Condensed_Matter_Theory "Institute for Condensed Matter Theory") (ICMT) was launched, with the director [Paul Goldbart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Goldbart "Paul Goldbart") and the chief scientist [Anthony Leggett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Leggett "Anthony Leggett"). ICMT is located at the Engineering Science Building on campus.

### Notable discoveries and innovations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Notable discoveries and innovations")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ab/GraingerEngineeringLibrary.jpg/250px-GraingerEngineeringLibrary.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GraingerEngineeringLibrary.jpg)

[Grainger Engineering Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grainger_Engineering_Library "Grainger Engineering Library")

In the field of natural sciences, the [BCS theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BCS_theory "BCS theory"), a groundbreaking theory of [superconductivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superconductivity "Superconductivity"), was proposed by [John Bardeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bardeen "John Bardeen") in collaboration with [Leon Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Cooper "Leon Cooper") and his doctoral student [John Robert Schrieffer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Robert_Schrieffer "John Robert Schrieffer"). Their work earned them the [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") in 1972.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-washpost-117) In the realm of agricultural science, John Laughnan, while a professor, developed [sweet corn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet_corn#Genetics "Sweet corn") with higher-than-normal sugar content, a significant advancement in crop science.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-DLLarson-118)

In computer and applied sciences, several notable achievements originated from the University of Illinois. The [ILLIAC I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ILLIAC_I "ILLIAC I"), built in 1952, was the first computer entirely constructed and owned by a U.S. educational institution. It was also used by [Lejaren Hiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lejaren_Hiller "Lejaren Hiller") and [Leonard Issacson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Issacson "Leonard Issacson") to create the _[Illiac Suite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illiac\_Suite "Illiac Suite")_, the first known composition written by an electronic computer.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Baggi-120) The development of [LLVM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LLVM "LLVM"), initially started by [Vikram Adve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_Adve "Vikram Adve") and [Chris Lattner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Lattner "Chris Lattner"), is now recognized as a major project in compiler infrastructure.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-121) Another milestone was the development of the [Mosaic web browser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosaic_(web_browser) "Mosaic (web browser)") at the [National Center for Supercomputing Applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Center_for_Supercomputing_Applications "National Center for Supercomputing Applications") in 1993.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-mosaic_and_th_w3-122)

[NAMD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAMD "NAMD"), a molecular dynamics simulation code, was pioneered by [Klaus Schulten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klaus_Schulten "Klaus Schulten") and his team at the Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology, further advancing computational biophysics. The [PLATO system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLATO_(computer_system) "PLATO (computer system)"), also developed at the University of Illinois, was the first generalized [computer assisted instruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_assisted_instruction "Computer assisted instruction") system, which by the late 1970s supported thousands of terminals globally, introducing many concepts foundational to modern multi-user computing such as forums, instant messaging, and online testing.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-124) In terms of interface technologies, [Donald Bitzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Bitzer "Donald Bitzer") was instrumental in the 1960s development of both [touchscreens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchscreen "Touchscreen") and [plasma displays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_display "Plasma display").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-125) Furthermore, Doug Brown and David R. Woolley created [Talkomatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talkomatic "Talkomatic") in 1973 on the PLATO system, an early online chat system enabling real-time text communication among small groups.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-126)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-FalkDrayton-127)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Bidgoli2004-128)

In the realm of audio-visual technology, [Joseph Tykociński-Tykociner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Tykoci%C5%84ski-Tykociner "Joseph Tykociński-Tykociner") publicly demonstrated for the first time a motion picture with a soundtrack optically recorded directly onto the film in 1922.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-129)

#### Student government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Student government")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/%222010%22_University_of_Illinois.jpg/250px-%222010%22_University_of_Illinois.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%222010%22_University_of_Illinois.jpg)

[Foellinger Auditorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foellinger_Auditorium "Foellinger Auditorium")

U of I has an extensive history of past student governments. Two years after the university opened in 1868, John Milton Gregory and a group of students created a constitution for a student government. Their governance expanded to the entire university in 1873, having a legislative, executive, and judicial branch. For a period of time, this government had the ability to discipline students. In 1883, however, due to a combination of events from Gregory's resignation to student-faculty infighting, the government formally dissolved itself via [plebiscite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plebiscite "Plebiscite").[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-149)

It was not until 1934, when the Student Senate, the next university-wide student government, was created. A year before, future Illinois Dean of Students, Fred H. Turner and the university's Senate Committee on Student Affairs gave increased power to the Student Council, an organization primarily known for organizing dances. A year after, the Student Council created a constitution and became the Student Senate, under the oversight of the Committee on Student Affairs. This Student Senate would last for 35 years.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-150) The Student Senate changed its purpose and name in 1969, when it became the Undergraduate Student Association (UGSA). It ceased being a representational government, becoming a [collective bargaining agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective_bargaining_agency "Collective bargaining agency") instead. It often worked with the Graduate Student Association to work on various projects[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-151)

In 1967, [Bruce A. Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_A._Morrison "Bruce A. Morrison") and other U of I graduate founded the Graduate Student Association (GSA). GSA would last until 1978, when it merged with the UGSA to form the Champaign-Urbana Student Association (CUSA).[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-152)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-illinois1948-153) CUSA lasted for only two years when it was replaced by the Student Government Association (SGA) in 1980. SGA lasted for 15 years until it became the Illinois Student Government (ISG) in 1995. ISG lasted until 2004.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-illinois1948-153)

The current university student government, created in 2004, is the Illinois Student Senate, a combined undergraduate and graduate student senate with 54 voting members. The student senators are elected by college and represent the students in the Urbana-Champaign Senate (which comprises both faculty and students), as well as on a variety of faculty and administrative committees, and are led by an internally elected executive board of a president, external vice president, internal vice president, and treasurer. As of 2012[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit), the executive board is supported by an executive staff consisting of a chief of staff, clerk of the Senate, parliamentarian, director of communications, Intern Coordinator, and the historian of the Senate.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-154)

### Residence halls

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/BuseyHall_Urbana_Illinois_4543.jpg/250px-BuseyHall_Urbana_Illinois_4543.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BuseyHall_Urbana_Illinois_4543.jpg)

[Busey-Evans Residence Halls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busey-Evans_Residence_Halls "Busey-Evans Residence Halls") is one of many buildings on the [NRHP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRHP "NRHP").

The university provides housing for undergraduates through [24 residence halls in Urbana and Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campus_of_the_University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign#Residence_halls "Campus of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign"). Incoming freshmen are required to live in student housing (campus or certified) their first year on campus. The university also maintains two graduate residence halls, which are restricted to students who are sophomores or above, and three university-owned apartment complexes. Some undergraduates choose to move into apartments or the Greek houses after their first year. There are a number of private dormitories around campus, as well as 15 private, certified residences that partner with the university to offer a variety of different housing options, including ones that are cooperatives, single-gender or religiously affiliated.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-PCH16-155) U of I is known for being one of the first universities to provide accommodations for students with disabilities.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-Education_secretary_UI-156) In 2015, the University of Illinois announced that they would be naming its newest residence hall after [Carlos Montezuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Montezuma "Carlos Montezuma"), also known as Wassaja. He is the first [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") graduate, and is believed to be one of the first Native Americans to receive a medical degree.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-157)

Among universities in North America, only the collections of Harvard are larger.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-158) Currently, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's 20+ departmental libraries and divisions hold more than 24 [million](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million "Million") items, including more than 12 million print volumes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-illinois2-21)As of 2012[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit), it had also the largest "browsable" university library in the United States, with 5 million volumes directly accessible in stacks in a single location.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-159) The university also has the largest public engineering library ([Grainger Engineering Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grainger_Engineering_Library "Grainger Engineering Library")) in the country.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-160)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-illinois2-21)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-161) In addition to the main library building, which houses numerous subject-oriented libraries, the Isaac Funk Family Library on the South Quad serves the [College of Agriculture, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIUC_College_of_Agriculture,_Consumer,_and_Environmental_Sciences "UIUC College of Agriculture, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences") and the Grainger Engineering Library Information Center serves the [College of Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIUC_College_of_Engineering "UIUC College of Engineering") on the [John Bardeen Quad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIUC_Engineering_Campus "UIUC Engineering Campus").

The [Main Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Library_(University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign) "Main Library (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)"), which includes the [Rare Book & Manuscript Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rare_Book_&_Manuscript_Library_(University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign) "The Rare Book & Manuscript Library (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)")

Residence Hall Library System is one of three in the nation.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-162)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-163) The Residence Hall Libraries were created in 1948 to serve the educational, recreational, and cultural information needs of first- and second-year undergraduate students residing in the residence halls, and the living-learning communities within the residence halls. The collection also serves University Housing staff as well as the larger campus community.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-164)[The Rare Book & Manuscript Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rare_Book_&_Manuscript_Library_(University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign) "The Rare Book & Manuscript Library (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)") (RBML) is one of the [Special collections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_collections "Special collections") units within the University Library.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-165) The RBML is one of the largest special collections repositories in the United States.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-166)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-167)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-168)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-169)

The university has several museums, galleries, and archives which include [Krannert Art Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krannert_Art_Museum "Krannert Art Museum"), [Sousa Archives and Center for American Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sousa_Archives_and_Center_for_American_Music "Sousa Archives and Center for American Music") and [Spurlock Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spurlock_Museum "Spurlock Museum"). Gallery and exhibit locations include [Krannert Center for the Performing Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krannert_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "Krannert Center for the Performing Arts") and at [the School of Art and Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UIUC_College_of_Fine_and_Applied_Arts "UIUC College of Fine and Applied Arts").

The Illinois Open Publishing Network (IOPN) is hosted and coordinated by the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Library, offering publishing services to members of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign community, to disseminate [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access "Open access")[scholarly publications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholarly_publication "Scholarly publication").[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois#cite_note-170)

### Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/CUMTD_Bus_2105.jpg/250px-CUMTD_Bus_2105.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CUMTD_Bus_2105.jpg)

A [Champaign–Urbana Mass Transit District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign%E2%80%93Urbana_Mass_Transit_District "Champaign–Urbana Mass Transit District") (MTD) bus

The bus system that operates throughout the campus and community is operated by the [Champaign-Urbana Mass Transit District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champaign-Urbana_Mass_Transit_District "Champaign-Urbana Mass Transit District"). The MTD receives a student-approved transportation fee from the university, which provides [unlimited access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_transit_pass "Universal transit pass") for university students, faculty, and staff.

Daily [Amtrak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amtrak "Amtrak") trains through [Illinois Terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Terminal "Illinois Terminal") connect Champaign-Urbana with Chicago and [Carbondale, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbondale,_Illinois "Carbondale, Illinois"). This includes the corridor service _[Illini and Saluki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illini\_and\_Saluki "Illini and Saluki")_ and the long-distance _[City of New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City\_of\_New\_Orleans\_(train) "City of New Orleans (train)")_, which provides a direct route to [Memphis, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee"); [Jackson, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson,_Mississippi "Jackson, Mississippi"); and [New Orleans, Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans,_Louisiana "New Orleans, Louisiana") southbound, in addition to Chicago northbound.

[Willard Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Willard_Airport "University of Illinois Willard Airport"), opened in 1954 and is named for former University of Illinois president Arthur Cutts Willard. The airport is located in Savoy. Willard Airport is home to university research projects, along with flights from [American Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Airlines "American Airlines"). In 2013, the university's [Institute of Aviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Institute_of_Aviation "University of Illinois Institute of Aviation") was closed at the University of Illinois and the program was transferred to [Parkland College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkland_College_(United_States) "Parkland College (United States)").
